vulns.title: Flawed overflow guard in math_utils allows near-free liquidity
vulns.root_cause: checked_shl_64 guards its 2^64 left-shift with `n > overflow_mask` (overflow_mask = 0xFFFF..FF << 192 = 2^256 - 2^192) instead of `n >= 1 << 192`. For a numerator in the window [2^192, 2^256 - 2^192] the guard reports NO overflow and takes the shift branch, where `n << 64` wraps modulo 2^256 (the precision fallback is the safe path and is never reached). An attacker crafts sqrt-price bounds so `liquidity * (upper - lower)` is a multiple of 2^192; the wrap drives the numerator to 0, so compute_deposit_a returns required_a = 0 and add_liquidity mints a large-liquidity position for a zero token-A deposit. The minted position records deposited_a = 0, evidencing liquidity with no backing. Fix: guard on `n >= 1 << 192` and reject (abort) an out-of-band numerator rather than fall back to a wrong scale.
